questions.question: Where is Central Asian Football Association is head-quartered?
questions.questionHtml: Where is Central Asian Football Association is head-quartered?
questions.solution: The Central Asian Football Association (CAFA) is an association of the football playing nations in Central Asia. In June 2014, the association was in principle approved by the Asian Football Confederation and approved at the Extraordinary Congress in January 2015 during the 2015 AFC Asian Cup. As a result, CAFA will in the future be able to have member(s) on the AFC executive committee. The CAFA is head-quartered in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

questions.question: Which among the following countries is not a member of the Central Asian Football Association?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following countries is not a member of the Central Asian Football Association?
questions.solution: The Central Asian Football Association (CAFA) is an association of the football playing nations in Central Asia. CAFA will consist of six member associations. All of them are members of the Asian Football Confederation. The member countries are, Afghanistan, Iran, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

questions.question: Where is the Asian Football Confederation head-quartered?
questions.questionHtml: Where is the Asian Football Confederation head-quartered?
questions.solution: The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) is the governing body of association football in Asia and Australia. It has 47 member countries, mostly located on the Asian and Australian continent, but excludes the transcontinental countries with territory in both Europe and Asia - Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Russia, and Turkey - which are instead members of UEFA. One of FIFA's six continental confederations, the AFC was formed officially on 8 May 1954 in Manila, Philippines, on the side-lines of the second Asian Games. The main headquarters is located in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first cricketer to receive Arjuna Award?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was the first cricketer to receive Arjuna Award?
questions.solution: Salim Aziz Durani is a former Indian cricketer who played in 29 Tests from 1960 to 1973. He was the first cricketer to win an Arjuna Award. He was awarded the C.K. Nayudu Lifetime Achievement Award by the BCCI in 2011.

questions.question: The Santhosh Trophy is associated with which of the following sports?
questions.questionHtml: The Santhosh Trophy is associated with which of the following sports?
questions.solution: The Santosh Trophy is an association football knock-out competition contested by the regional state associations and government institutions under the All India Football Federation (AIFF), the sport's governing body in India. Before the start of the first national club league, the National Football League, in 1996, the Santosh Trophy was considered the top domestic championship in India. Many players who have represented India internationally played and gained notoriety while playing in the Santosh Trophy. The tournament is held every year with 31 teams who are divided into groups and who must qualify for the tournament proper through the preliminary round.

questions.question: B.C. Roy Trophy is associated with
questions.questionHtml: B.C. Roy Trophy is associated with
questions.solution: The BC Roy Trophy is an Indian football tournament for players under 19 years of age. The competition is held every year between the under-19 teams representing states of India.

questions.question: Ranji Trophy is associated with which of the following sports?
questions.questionHtml: Ranji Trophy is associated with which of the following sports?
questions.solution: The Ranji Trophy is a domestic first-class cricket championship played in India between teams representing regional cricket associations. The competition currently consists of 28 teams, with 21 of the 29 states in India and Delhi having at least one representation. The competition is named after first Indian cricketer who played international cricket, Ranjitsinhji, who was also known as "Ranji". He played for England and Sussex.

questions.question: Which among the following countries has hosted the commonwealth games for four or more times?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following countries has hosted the commonwealth games for four or more times?
questions.solution: Nine nations have hosted the Commonwealth Games. 18 cities in seven countries have hosted the event. Australia has hosted four Commonwealth Games (1938, 1962, 1982, 2006) and will host for the fifth time in 2018. Canada has hosted four Commonwealth Games (1930, 1954, 1978, 1994). Two cities have hosted Commonwealth Games more than one time: Auckland (1950, 1990) and Edinburgh (1970, 1986).

questions.question: In which among the following sports the rectangular court is not being used?
questions.questionHtml: In which among the following sports the rectangular court is not being used?
questions.solution: A baseball field, also called a ball field or a baseball diamond, is the field upon which the game of baseball is played. The term can also be used as a metonym for a baseball park.

questions.question: Which among the following is the highest governing body of cricket?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following is the highest governing body of cricket?
questions.solution: The International Cricket Council (ICC) is the international governing body of cricket. It was founded as the Imperial Cricket Conference in 1909 by representatives from England, Australia and South Africa, renamed the International Cricket Conference in 1965, and took up its current name in 1989.

questions.question: Gridiron football is also known as
questions.questionHtml: Gridiron football is also known as
questions.solution: Gridiron football, also known as North American football or simply football, is a football sport primarily played in the United States and Canada. American football, which uses 11-player teams, is the form played in the United States and the best known form worldwide, while Canadian football, featuring 12-player teams, predominates in Canada. Other derivative varieties include indoor football, football for smaller teams (most commonly eight players), and informal games such as touch and flag football. Football is played at professional, collegiate, semi-professional, and amateur levels.

questions.question: The national sport of Estonia is
questions.questionHtml: The national sport of Estonia is
questions.solution: National sport of Estonia is Basketball. Basketball is a limited contact sport played on a rectangular court. While most often played as a team sport with five players on each side, three-on-three, two-on-two, and one-on-one competitions are also common. The objective is to shoot a ball through a hoop 18 inches (46 cm) in diameter and 10 feet (3.048 m) high that is mounted to a backboard at each end of the court. The game was invented in 1891 by Dr. James Naismith.

questions.question: What is the national sport of Israel?
questions.questionHtml: What is the national sport of Israel?
questions.solution: Soccer (football) is the national sport of Israel. While Israel is technically part of Asia, the sporting landscape makes the tiny nation more in line with the European continent. Soccer rules in Israel, as it does in the rest of the non-American world, and while the country has its own hierarchy of professional leagues, Israeli teams often face European competition in international matches through UEFA (Union of European Football Associations).

questions.question: Which among the following is the national sport of Italy?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following is the national sport of Italy?
questions.solution: Football or soccer (calcio) is Italy's national sport and by far the most important in Italy, occupying almost the entire first half of each issue of La Gazzetta dello Sport. Italian football fans (tifosi) are among the most dedicated and fervent in Europe, matched in their fanaticism only by the English, Scottish and Spanish.

questions.question: How many medal/s won by India in Olympic games in their first appearance?
questions.questionHtml: How many medal/s won by India in Olympic games in their first appearance?
questions.solution: Norman Pritchard was the first Indian athlete to participate in the Olympic Games and was also the first to win an Olympic medal and also represent an Asian nation. He won two silver medals at the 1900 Summer Olympics in Paris, coming second in the 200 metres behind Walter Tewksbury of the United States and second in the 200 metres hurdles behind the legendary Alvin Kraenzlein, also of the United States. He reached the final of the 110 metres hurdles, but did not finish, and also participated in the 60 metres and 100 metres sprints, in which he failed to qualify for the finals.

questions.question: Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore has secured a silver medal by participated in the double trap event of shooting of which among the following editions of Olympic games?
questions.questionHtml: Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore has secured a silver medal by participated in the double trap event of shooting of which among the following editions of Olympic games?
questions.solution: Colonel Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore AVSM is an Indian politician and a former professional shooter. As a shooter, competing in the double trap event, he won a silver medal in the 2004 Olympic Games. In a career spanning over a decade, he also won multiple medals at the Commonwealth and Asian Games.

questions.question: Pankaj Advani is associated with which sports?
questions.questionHtml: Pankaj Advani is associated with which sports?
questions.solution: Pankaj Arjan Advani is an Indian professional player of English billiards and former professional snooker player. In recognition of his achievements, the Government of India has bestowed several awards upon Advani - Arjuna Award in 2004, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in 2006, and Padma Shri in 2009.

questions.question: Vijender Singh has secured the bronze medal in 2008 Beijing Olympics in which among the following sport categories?
questions.questionHtml: Vijender Singh has secured the bronze medal in 2008 Beijing Olympics in which among the following sport categories?
questions.solution: Vijender Singh Beniwal, is an Indian professional boxer and the current WBO Asia Pacific Super Middleweight Champion and WBO Oriental Super Middleweight Champion from Kaluwas, Bhiwani district in Haryana. Having won medals in different competitions at the national level, Vijender was picked to train and compete at several international level competitions such as the 2004 Athens Summer Olympics and the 2006 Commonwealth Games. At the 2006 Asian Games in Doha, he won the bronze medal after losing the semi-final bout against Kazakhstan's Bakhtiyar Artayev. At the 2008 Beijing Summer Olympics, he defeated Carlos Gongora of Ecuador 9 - 4 in the quarterfinals which garnered him a bronze medal - the first ever Olympic medal for an Indian boxer.

questions.question: Indian wrestler Sushil Kumar has secured Olympic silver medal which among the following editions?
questions.questionHtml: Indian wrestler Sushil Kumar has secured Olympic silver medal which among the following editions?
questions.solution: Sushil Kumar is an Indian freestyle wrestler. Competing in the 66 kg weight division he won the 2010 world title, a silver medal at the 2012 London Olympics and a bronze medal at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, which made him the only Indian to win two individual Olympic medals. His 2008 Olympic medal was second for India in wrestling, and the first since Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav's bronze medal at the 1952 Summer Olympics. In July 2009, he received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna - India's highest honour for sportspersons.

questions.question: A team of Baseball game consists of how many players?
questions.questionHtml: A team of Baseball game consists of how many players?
questions.solution: Baseball is a bat-and-ball game played between two teams of nine players each, who take turns batting and fielding. The batting team attempts to score runs by hitting a ball (that is thrown by the opposing team's pitcher) with a bat swung by the batter, and then running counter-clockwise around a series of four bases: first, second, third, and home plate. A run is scored when a player advances around the bases and returns to home plate.

questions.question: What is the official distance of marathon?
questions.questionHtml: What is the official distance of marathon?
questions.solution: The marathon is a long-distance running race with an official distance of 42.195 kilometres (26.219 miles, or 26 miles 385 yards), usually run as a road race. The event was instituted in commemoration of the fabled run of the Greek soldier Pheidippides, a messenger from the Battle of Marathon to Athens, who reported the victory.

questions.question: David Lloyd is the former cricketer of which among the following countries?
questions.questionHtml: David Lloyd is the former cricketer of which among the following countries?
questions.solution: David Lloyd is an English former cricketer who played county cricket for Lancashire and Test and One Day International cricket for England. He also played semi-professional football for Accrington Stanley. He is known through the cricketing world as "Bumble" because of the ostensible similarity between his facial profile and those of the Bumblies, characters of Michael Bentine's children's television programmes.

questions.question: Hisense Arena is the tennis stadium located in which country?
questions.questionHtml: Hisense Arena is the tennis stadium located in which country?
questions.solution: The Melbourne Park Multi-Purpose Venue, currently also known by its sponsorship name as Hisense Arena, is an Australian sports venue that is part of the National Tennis Centre at Melbourne Park in Melbourne, Victoria.

questions.question: The Monte-Carlo Masters tennis tournament is played in which among the following courts?
questions.questionHtml: The Monte-Carlo Masters tennis tournament is played in which among the following courts?
questions.solution: The Monte-Carlo Masters is an annual tennis tournament for male professional players held in Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, France, a commune that borders on Monaco. The event is part of the ATP World Tour Masters 1000 on the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) Tour. The tournament is played on clay courts and is held every year in the April - May period.

questions.question: Olympic gold medallist Michael Phelps hails from which country?
questions.questionHtml: Olympic gold medallist Michael Phelps hails from which country?
questions.solution: Michael Fred Phelps II is an American retired competitive swimmer and the most successful and most decorated Olympian of all time, with a total of 28 medals. Phelps also holds the all-time records for Olympic gold medals (23), Olympic gold medals in individual events (13), and Olympic medals in individual events (16).

questions.question: Luzhniki Stadium is located in which among the following countries?
questions.questionHtml: Luzhniki Stadium is located in which among the following countries?
questions.solution: Luzhniki Stadium, is a sports stadium in Moscow, Russia. Its total seating capacity is 81,000 seats, all covered (upgraded). The stadium is a part of the Luzhniki Olympic Complex, and is located in Khamovniki District of the Central Administrative Okrug of Moscow city.

questions.question: Rose Bowl is located in which country?
questions.questionHtml: Rose Bowl is located in which country?
questions.solution: The Rose Bowl is an outdoor athletic stadium in Pasadena, California, just outside Los Angeles. Built in 1922 among the San Gabriel Mountains in the Arroyo Seco of Los Angeles County, the stadium is recognized as a United States National Historic Landmark and a California Historic Civil Engineering landmark.

questions.question: Formula one racing driver Fernando Alonso hails from which country?
questions.questionHtml: Formula one racing driver Fernando Alonso hails from which country?
questions.solution: Fernando Alonso Díaz About this sound audio is a Spanish Formula One racing driver and a double World Champion who is currently racing for McLaren-Honda. He is often regarded as one of the greatest Formula One drivers in the history of the sport. He took part in the 2017 Indianapolis 500.

questions.question: In 1999 Anil Kumble dismissed all the ten batsmen in a Test match innings. He reached this milestone while playing against which country?
questions.questionHtml: In 1999 Anil Kumble dismissed all the ten batsmen in a Test match innings. He reached this milestone while playing against which country?
questions.solution: Anil Kumble is a former Indian cricketer and a former captain of Tests and ODIs, who played Tests and ODIs for 18 years. A right-arm leg spin (leg break googly) bowler, he took 619 wickets in Test cricket and remains the third-highest wicket taker of all time (as of 2017, behind Muttiah Muralitharan and Shane Warne). In 1999 while playing against Pakistan, Kumble dismissed all the ten batsmen in a Test match innings, being among the only two players to achieve this feat; the other player being Jim Laker of England.
